title: Cross-SDK release pipeline: atomic publishing, provenance signing, and CI gating for Python/TS/Go
creator: Avery Cho
description:
Goal: implement a unified, auditable, and atomic release pipeline for all official Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) that enforces semantic versioning, produces provenance evidence, signs published artifacts, and is gated by CI checks and cross-SDK compatibility tests.

Background: Currently each SDK repo has ad-hoc release steps: semantic-release for TS, manual twine uploads for Python, and manual tagging for Go. This leads to inconsistencies in versions, lack of unified provenance, and occasional mistaken releases. We need a reproducible pipeline that: (1) ensures an all-or-nothing publish across languages for cross-cutting breaking changes; (2) provides cryptographically verifiable provenance (sigstore/cosign/in-toto) for compliance and incident investigation; (3) integrates with existing KMS/HSM for key management; (4) automates common versioning and rollbacks.

Proposed approach summary:
- Versioning: SemVer for all SDKs (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Maintain a single source-of-truth compatibility matrix in the sdk-compatibility repo. Use semantic-release for TS, python-semantic-release (or bump2version) for Python, and goreleaser for Go. Tagging must be canonical on the main repo.
- Atomic publish orchestration: Create a GitHub Actions workflow in the release-orchestrator repo that: checks PRs merged into main, computes candidate versions per SDK from changelogs/commits, runs cross-SDK integration matrix, builds artifacts (wheel/sdist, npm tgz, go module tag), signs artifacts, and only when all artifacts succeed, performs final publish step in a single transaction (publish to test registries then promotion to production registries).
- Provenance and signing: Use Sigstore (fulcio + rekor + cosign) as primary signing provenance system for all three artifact types. For PyPI, also emit and upload detached PGP signatures (.asc) for compatibility. For npm, create tarballs and sign with cosign; attach Rekor attestation in the GitHub Release. For Go, sign the git tags and release assets using cosign/gpg and produce in-toto attestations for the build steps. Store signing keys in customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS + AWS CloudHSM or GCP KMS) with short-lived ephemeral keys via GitHub OIDC.
- CI gating: Enforce the following checks before publishing: unit tests, linters, integration smoke tests against mock Redwood API, cross-SDK compatibility matrix tests, reproducible build verification (same artifact checksum across two independent runners), and provenance verification.
- Publishing flow: (1) create release candidate (RC) artifacts and sign, (2) push RC artifacts to test registries (test.pypi.org / npm registry under @redwood-inference/rc / internal go proxy), (3) run acceptance tests against RCs, (4) if green, run final publish job to production registries. Final publish must be a single orchestrated job so partial publishes do not occur.

Acceptance criteria:
- All three SDKs are published through the orchestrator release workflow by 2026-03-25.
- Every published artifact has a Sigstore entry (Rekor) and a downloadable attestation in the GitHub Release.
- CI blocks publishing if cross-SDK matrix tests fail.
- Audit playbook documented for revoking/rolling back a release and tracing provenance.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Registry constraints (PyPI removal is slow). Mitigation: prefer deprecation + yanking metadata in registry and internal blacklist; coordinate with support if removal required.
- Risk: Key compromise. Mitigation: use OIDC + KMS, short-lived keys, and hardware-backed keys where required; ensure key rotation runbook.
- Risk: Breaking changes accidentally released across SDKs. Mitigation: require compatibility matrix job and manual approver for major-version bumps.

Notes on implementation decisions:
- We recommend Sigstore as the canonical provenance mechanism to avoid managing a bespoke PKI for multiple ecosystems. Sigstore works for arbitrary artifacts and integrates with Rekor transparency logs for tamper-evident records.
- Semantic-release remains the best tool for TS because of existing conventional commit policies; for Python we evaluated python-semantic-release (works well) vs. bump2version; chosen: python-semantic-release for integration parity. For Go, goreleaser handles cross-platform artifacts and tags.
- For npm 2FA and token safety: use ephemeral publish tokens minted by the orchestrator using a scoped machine account and rotate daily.

Deliverables:
- GitHub Actions workflows in release-orchestrator: build-and-sign-rc.yml and publish-atomic-final.yml
- SDK changes: small release-hooks and a canonical VERSION file in each SDK repo
- Confluence runbook: "SDK Release + Provenance Playbook"
- Smoke test suite: cross-sdk-integration/tests (matrix against RCs)
- Monitoring/alerting: release-failure Slack channel and PagerDuty escalation for publish failures

comments: 2026-01-25: Kickoff meeting: agreed on single orchestrator approach instead of independent per-repo jobs. Action: Mateo to prototype orchestrator job.
2026-02-02: Prototype completed that builds wheels and npm tgz; sign step currently uses a developer PGP key (temporary) — need KMS/OIDC integration before final publish.
2026-02-12: Security requested Sigstore + KMS (approved). Created tickets for KMS onboarding (ENG-9120).
2026-02-20: Cross-SDK smoke tests flaked due to environment variable mismatch in TS SDK. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/142 merged.

2026-02-28: Ran first RC against test registries. Observed non-deterministic wheel build checksums across runners. Action: add reproducible-build step using manylinux build container and pinned buildenv.
2026-03-05: Design review with PM and Security. Decision: keep PGP detached signatures for PyPI in addition to Sigstore attestations to support downstream consumers that expect .asc files.

2026-03-09: Orchestrator final publish job added gating: cross-sdk tests + manual approver for MAJOR version bumps. Tests green for RC-0.1.6-rc. Next: run final publish to prod on 2026-03-11 (scheduled).
2026-03-10: Security review completed. Requirement: retention policy for Rekor entries documented; added to Confluence runbook.
next_steps: Finish KMS OIDC integration, run two full production publishes in sandbox, finalize runbook and training for release owners, and onboard platform on-call to publication failures runbook.
